entries.stability_scope: Top-level text stability is conservative for the mixed attach/detach command; the detached-summary-row surface is stable, while the attached raw-pty-stream has no stable sanitized text contract. Every spawned child process receives LTERM_SESSION and LTERM_PANE identity variables for in-session prompt badges and environment-aware tooling.

Run is an attached command surface: the raw-pty-stream sub-surface is transparent and intentionally has no stable sanitized text or JSON contract. Every spawned child process receives LTERM_SESSION and LTERM_PANE identity variables for in-session prompt badges and environment-aware tooling.

Resume/attach is a mixed surface: raw-pty-stream is transparent; local-status-bar is a client-side decoration; mobile-transcript is a non-attached sanitized capture/send UI and must not resize or register as an attached client. Explicit --mobile / LTERM_ATTACH_MODE=mobile selection exposes the stable mobile-transcript sub-surface; automatic mobile selection remains conservative best-effort policy. The agent-presence-cue sub-surface is a host-side best-effort compact terminal-title cue (`lt:<session>:<pane> · <agent>`) plus sanitized one-shot banner emitted before raw attach for row-off agent sessions, with idle title-only refresh while attached row-off; it does not filter or rewrite the attached PTY stream and is controlled by LTERM_AGENT_CUE / LTERM_AGENT_BANNER.

Open is a mixed attach-or-create surface: create-if-missing-control covers local control behavior before attach; raw-pty-stream is transparent; mobile-transcript is a non-attached sanitized capture/send UI and must not resize or register as an attached client. Explicit --mobile / LTERM_ATTACH_MODE=mobile selection exposes the stable mobile-transcript sub-surface; automatic mobile selection remains conservative best-effort policy. The agent-presence-cue sub-surface is a host-side best-effort compact terminal-title cue (`lt:<session>:<pane> · <agent>`) plus sanitized one-shot banner emitted before raw attach for row-off agent sessions, with idle title-only refresh while attached row-off; it does not filter or rewrite the attached PTY stream and is controlled by LTERM_AGENT_CUE / LTERM_AGENT_BANNER.

Reconnect is a mixed attach surface: last-session-pointer is a private best-effort local target-selection hint stored under the user-private lterm data dir. It stores only session_id, pane_id, the user-provided session_name, and a timestamp; it must not include derived command lines, cwd, scrollback, URLs, host metadata, or secrets. Users should not put secrets in session names. Stale, corrupt, or missing pointers fall back to the explicit fallback target, defaulting to main when omitted. raw-pty-stream remains transparent after target selection; mobile-transcript is a non-attached sanitized capture/send UI and must not resize or register as an attached client. Explicit --mobile / LTERM_ATTACH_MODE=mobile selection exposes the stable mobile-transcript sub-surface; --read-only never creates a missing fallback target.

Exits is a bounded raw-free recent-session lifecycle evidence report. It exposes only opaque session identity, sanitized hierarchy/profile fields, lifecycle timestamps, trigger/outcome/evidence enums, and optional exit code or sanitized signal. It excludes command, cwd, environment, PTY bytes, scrollback, tokens, and process identifiers. The daemon caps --limit at 100 and applies top-level/children/all scope before returning newest-first rows.

Instrument is a read-only, raw-free generic RPC and requires --json. It never attaches, captures, traces, parses, sanitizes, or rewrites PTY bytes. Only output_closed, output_revision, and output_total_bytes are copied together; identity, alive, attached_clients, rows, and cols are relaxed independent samples rather than one transactional snapshot. The exact schema contains only opaque identity, booleans, counters, geometry, and observation time; it excludes name, command, cwd, environment, captured text, and raw terminal-derived content.

Capability is an opt-in cooperative input attenuation surface inside the existing same-UID trust boundary, not a sandbox. Tokens exist only in validated private files and a same-connection v5 sensitive frame; raw Attach and legacy Send remain unchanged. Attempt bytes are atomically charged before one PTY write and are not refunded on failure.

Metadata is a protocol-v6, raw-free, live-session-only linear journal for name and status_theme. It hard-rejects new mutations behind the tip or at 1024 entries without branch truncation or eviction; no-ops still succeed. Undo/redo validate the whole current pair and rename index before atomic commit. Purge requires --irreversible plus the exact canonical live session UUID, preserves current metadata, and clears only volatile history; it is an accident gate, not authorization or durable audit. Raw Attach, legacy Send, Kill, close, and process/filesystem effects are not reversible and remain unchanged.

Init is a no-touch setup preview for humans. It prints recommended commands and optional reversible mobile reconnect profile snippets guarded by LTERM_RECONNECT_DISABLE=1, and must not modify shell startup files or daemon state.

Urls is a sanitized scrollback report surface. It scans the last --tail sanitized lines, never attaches to or rewrites the raw PTY stream, prints stable numbered text rows by default, and emits a stable JSON string array for --json. Extraction matches http:// and https:// schemes ASCII-case-insensitively while preserving the original URL text. Text and JSON consume the same extracted URL set: first-seen exact-text deduplicated unique ASCII URL tokens capped at 256 rows, complete raw URL candidates longer than 4096 bytes skipped before trimming instead of truncated, and whitespace/control-bearing or non-ASCII tokens excluded. --last emits the newest valid within-length URL occurrence in the captured tail, even if that occurrence is a duplicate or appears after the 256-row unique-list cap; --last --json emits [] or a one-element array. Empty text modes produce no rows; empty JSON mode produces []. Extracted URLs are untrusted terminal output and may include phishing links or short-lived authentication secrets; automation should treat URL rows as sensitive and avoid logging them verbatim by default.

Search is a sanitized scrollback report surface. It scans the last --tail sanitized lines, defaults to --tail 120, never attaches to or rewrites the raw PTY stream, and performs case-sensitive literal line matching. Text output is stable 1-based numbered rows as N<TAB>LINE in capture order. --json emits the same fully sanitized matching line strings as a JSON array. Empty result text mode produces no rows; empty result JSON mode produces []. Empty QUERY is rejected before reporting. Matching lines are untrusted terminal output and are sanitized before matching and rendering.

Opt-in private local JSONL trace file for debugging raw PTY output. It records raw output bytes as hex, caps raw capture with --max-bytes, and does not replay bytes to stdout; exact JSONL fields are best-effort until a stable trace schema is promoted.
Explicitly decodes a local lterm trace JSONL file and writes recorded raw PTY output bytes to stdout. It does not connect to the daemon or sanitize replayed bytes.
Summarizes lterm trace JSONL metadata and aggregate chunk counts without printing raw bytes_hex payloads. Exact field names are best-effort until a stable trace summary schema is promoted.

compose/mobile is a non-attached local composer, not a machine-readable report surface. The top-level sanitized-output-only policy applies to displayed scrollback only. The composer layout is best-effort, while the displayed capture text is a stable sanitized-capture-display sub-surface. The display resolves targets like logs and captures the last --tail sanitized lines (default 80); --once captures once before commit, while interactive mode refreshes on --refresh (default 500ms), local input, and terminal resize. Committed text is sent through the existing input/send path: default commits append Enter (carriage return), --no-enter sends exact message bytes, interactive Enter uses the same default rule even for an empty buffer, and compose must not subscribe to attach, resize, or alter attached-client counts or PTY geometry. The --transcript sub-surface uses the same normal-screen transcript display as explicit mobile attach: sanitized capture output, optional read-only follow mode, and no raw attach subscription; automatic mobile attach selection is not part of the compose/mobile contract. Transcript-local commands /refresh, /raw, /links, /urls, /grep QUERY, /exit, and /quit are local controls and are not forwarded to the PTY; unrecognized transcript input is sent through the committed-input path. /links and /urls reuse the URL extraction surface locally and print `No URLs found in current transcript.` when the current sanitized transcript has no links. /grep QUERY reuses the search surface locally over the active transcript --tail window (default 80), ignores only separator whitespace after /grep, keeps the remaining query literal, prints stable N<TAB>LINE rows, prints `Usage: /grep QUERY` when no query is provided, and prints `No matches found in current transcript.` when the current sanitized transcript has no matching lines.

Doctor JSON includes stable daemon/shim/version/path fields plus an additive optional tmux_compat object emitted by current builds, containing local command coverage counts and PATH-order boolean/null indicators only; the schema keeps tmux_compat optional so older stable doctor outputs still validate during mixed-version upgrades. It does not run arbitrary real tmux commands and does not include raw PTY bytes or scrollback.

Local-only redacted diagnostic bundle for issue reports and handoffs. It excludes raw PTY bytes and scrollback by default, does not auto-start the daemon, includes tmux compatibility data derived from local lterm metadata/PATH booleans without running arbitrary real tmux commands, and may evolve fields before being promoted to a stable JSON schema.

Inspect is an inspect-style JSON entrypoint for the same local-only redacted diagnostic bundle as diagnose --bundle. It requires --json, does not auto-start the daemon, excludes raw PTY bytes and scrollback by default, and may evolve fields before stable schema promotion.
Stable shell-eval semantics and exported variable names for default POSIX output and fish output requested with --shell fish; exact quote style and visual formatting are not stable.

Generates bash, zsh, and fish shell completion scripts from the current clap command surface. The command must not start the daemon; exact completion script bytes are delegated to clap-complete and are not a stable visual contract.

Writes a user-local bash, zsh, or fish completion file and prints a sanitized activation hint. The command must not start the daemon; completion script bytes are delegated to clap-complete and user shell discovery is best-effort.

Installs supported AI CLI statusline integrations with backup and idempotency safeguards. Claude/OMC command statusline configuration renders LTERM_SESSION/LTERM_PANE identity inside the AI CLI's own HUD. Codex config is left untouched and reported as skipped because current Codex status_line items are built-in only, and thread-id is Codex-internal rather than an lterm session identifier.
SSH is a mixed remote invocation surface: raw-pty-stream remains transparent after remote attach, while ssh-invocation covers local command construction and is not a raw output stream.

Agent launchers are mixed surfaces: raw-pty-stream is transparent once raw-attached; launcher-control covers local profile/session setup and persists optional agent metadata; mobile-transcript is a non-attached sanitized capture/send UI and must not resize or register as an attached client. Explicit --mobile / LTERM_ATTACH_MODE=mobile selection exposes the stable mobile-transcript sub-surface; automatic mobile selection remains conservative best-effort policy. The agent-presence-cue sub-surface is a host-side best-effort compact terminal-title cue (`lt:<session>:<pane> · <agent>`) plus sanitized one-shot banner emitted before raw attach when the launcher uses the default row-off full-height TUI surface; while attached row-off, idle refreshes re-emit only the title cue so Codex-like TUIs can own the screen without permanently erasing identity; LTERM_AGENT_CUE disables both cue forms and LTERM_AGENT_BANNER disables only the inline banner. Agent-spawned child processes also receive LTERM_SESSION and LTERM_PANE identity variables; this is covered by the generic agent profile environment test.
